hero_title: Save your AI for the real work.
hero_lede: Agents don't jam because the agents aren't smart enough. They jam from toe-stepping on the same files: who has the file, whose copy is stale, what passed testing first? what merged first?, which tests to run. codeSplitter takes those points over coordinating your code, your git, your humans, your agents. Unclog the git and code pipeline. Spends less tokens on the feature. Still hook in AI wherever along the way. We aren't promising to solve all the problems. We just want to solve the solveables so that you can focus on features not merge conflicts, testing fights, coordination fights, or even fighting continuing to work when the other git place is busy!
scene_unclog_title: Unclog the file for humans and agents
scene_unclog_text: With the old way, agents or humans take the whole file and fight over it on the way back to git. Here every line is its own record. Each one lands its own lines and nobody waits if nobody conflicts. codeSplitter just coordinates and fixes the fixable to make your conflicts disappear!
scene_drift_title: Branch at lightning speed. Avoid the noise.
scene_drift_text: Make git branches a real git repo in milliseconds. If left alone, copies would drift out of tune: their waves cancel, the signal diminishes, the light dims. Work leaks out of line. You, your AI, whomever gets pulled off features, security and maintenance and into the git plumbing: merge fights. Rewriting what someone just rewrote. Infighting and toe-stepping solveable problems. Watch the scope on the page.
scene_lock_title: Coordinate the file and the signal comes BACK!
scene_lock_text: Keep one live copy of each file and have Mervin settle the merges so that you do not have to. Now the harmonics line up and boost each other! The light gets bright, the energy gets through! AI checks in, finds nothing the matter, and goes back to features, security and maintenance. Once again plug in the AI, but now it gets to fight less and do more!
scene_mervin_title: Mervin settles the merges before they conflict you!
scene_mervin_text: Not a model: just a script man on a mission to de-conflict the space going as fast as the computer goes. Changes that don't clash go together in one wave. Ones that do clash wait a wave; rare real clashes come back as one card to solve.
scene_hook_title: Hook your AI in. Don't hook in your AI. We help human and AI coordination.
scene_hook_text: After Mervin, before Ester, after Ester: three places a hook can say yay or nay. Use the AI where and when it's judgement, and not traffic.
scene_ester_title: Ester the Tester stacks the tests in lanes
scene_ester_text: Some tests might just need to run on every change. Some every fifth. Testing can add up with agent swarms. Maybe you only need some tests closer to a preview release? Maybe just no tests at all? Ester just tries to take what you want into account and stack the test bus full. Not every piece of everything needs an all-the-time test if not attached to releases especially when you can do a larger later AI pass over a large change block vs 100x more often. Stack however much of however often the bus you want and notice patterns and suggest things to help is Ester's job. Also not AI, just some good-natured token saving, time saving, test saving computer magic!
scene_yours_text: Just hook in AI on steps and places you need or want it. Otherwise let Coordination, Mervin, and Ester come say your agentic swarm token use. Try to help with every stop on the way being whatever efficient tool call of the months: CLI, API, MCP, WebMCP, code mode. Human-friendly, agent-friendly, collaboration-friendly.
road_title: The git path has a change:
road_blurb: Every change, an agent's or a person's, goes down the same road. Each stop is deterministic: same inputs, same answer, no model, no tokens. The dashed ones are where your AI can say yay or nay.
stop_branch_text:
A branch is a real git repo, made in milliseconds. A thousand agents can each have one.

On its own, every copy starts drifting from the others the moment it's made.
stop_coordinate_text:
Each file's lines live in one place, on a tiny computer every agent talks to. Edits land in order, line by line, so nobody fights over a file and nobody waits on someone else's copy.

Watch the dots
stop_mervin_text:
Merges by line id. Changes that don't clash go together in one wave, the ones that do wait a wave, and the rare real clash comes back as a card.

His case file
stop_hook1_text: Review the merged change, or have the last word before the tests spend anything. Off, ai or ask.
stop_ester_text:
Runs only the lanes this change calls for, and sorts any red by whose it is: main's, flaky, the PR's own, or the merge's.

Her case file
stop_hook2_text: It's green. Does an AI or a person still want to look before it ships?
stop_yours_text: Ship it, deploy it, release it. From here on it's yours, however you like to work.
lanes_title: Test lanes: not every test, every time
lanes_blurb: Running every test on every change is how a swarm waits on its slowest suite. Ester gives each set of tests a cadence instead.
lane_always_runs: every change that touches its paths
lane_always_for: the tests you never want to go without
lane_often_runs: every Nth change, and at every release; the skipped ones are owed
lane_often_for: the slow ones that add up: stress runs, the end-to-end journey
lane_release_runs: only when a release is cut
lane_release_for: what you don't care about until then: the iOS app, two days before the preview
lane_bus_runs: no tests per change. Changes take a seat, and when it's full (or a release is cut) the bus leaves: one big pass over all of them, an AI's if the lane has no command
lane_bus_for: docs, copy, the long tail nobody tests by hand
config_file: A repo keeps its road in codesplitter.pipeline.json at the top of main. Without one: no hooks, one lane that tests everything.
config_ask: Then ask what a change does, from wherever you work. The same plain answer each time.
config_answer: The answer lists every stop, the hooks that are on, and each lane's call (run, skip, board or depart), with the counts to send with the next change. The API reference · MCP
why_title: Why the AI goes around the stops
why_text: Whether two edits touch the same line, or whether a red check was already red on main, is a lookup, not a judgement. A model would spend tokens and minutes on it, and every agent behind it waits. So the lookups are code, and the hooks hand an AI or a person only what is truly a judgement call: is this change right, is it ready, should it ship. The git problems a swarm hits · a real week of 1,000 PRs
